candidates.change_summary: Replace the assignment to owner with assigning the zero address, so transferOwnership always sets owner to address(0).
Replace the assignment to owner with assigning msg.sender, so transferOwnership sets owner to the caller rather than the provided newOwner.
Delete the assignment statement so transferOwnership no longer updates owner.
Insert a require that newOwner must not be zero, which can revert and thus prevent owner from changing in some calls.
Change the onlyOwner modifier to check owner != msg.sender instead of equality, inverting the guard so only non-owners can execute transferOwnership.
Change the onlyOwner modifier to require msg.sender be the zero address, so only the zero address may call transferOwnership (practically blocking normal calls).
Delete the require check inside onlyOwner, removing the ownership check so anyone can call transferOwnership.
Insert assignment to owner inside owned() so calling owned() changes the owner state.
Replace require in onlyOwner with a no-op (removed check), allowing anyone to call owned() and thus potentially change owner via owned if owned mutates state.
Insert a state-changing assignment in the onlyOwner modifier so that any function using it (including owned) will modify owner as a side effect.
Removed the onlyOwner guard by deleting the modifier invocation on transferOwnership so anyone can change owner.
Changed onlyOwner modifier to require the caller is NOT the owner, reversing the access check so transferOwnership can be called only by non-owners.
Altered transferOwnership to set owner to address(0) regardless of the provided newOwner, changing observed post-call owner value.
